title: Unconditional Advantage Of Quantum Teleportation Over Direct Transmission Of Single Photons Through A Lossy Channel
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration that quantum teleportation achieves higher state transfer efficiency than direct single-photon transmission through a lossy channel.
motivation: Quantum teleportation is a key primitive for quantum networks, but its advantage over direct transmission in realistic lossy channels had not been experimentally verified.
method: The authors perform a controlled experiment comparing teleportation of single-photon states using entangled pairs versus direct transmission through an equivalent lossy channel, measuring the fidelity and efficiency of state transfer.
result: Teleportation yields a higher success probability and fidelity than direct transmission under the same loss conditions, demonstrating an unconditional advantage.
conclusion: Quantum teleportation can outperform direct transmission in lossy channels, validating its use for long-distance quantum communication and network applications.

title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A photonic integrated quantum network using twin-field QKD over 540 km fiber with full connectivity between four users.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network using integrated photonics and twin-field QKD.
method: A spine-leaf network architecture with four users connected via a central node, using twin-field QKD at 1.25 GHz clock rate over up to 540 km fiber.
result: Achieved a secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of integrated photonic quantum networks for long-distance secure communication.

title: Analytical Computation Of Entanglement Distribution Time In First-generation Quantum Repeater Chains
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Analytical computation of entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains.
motivation: Understanding the time required to distribute entanglement over long distances is crucial for designing efficient quantum networks.
method: The paper develops an analytical model for the entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains, considering probabilistic entanglement swapping and purification.
result: Closed-form expressions for the distribution time are derived, showing scaling with chain length and repeater parameters.
conclusion: The analytical results enable optimization of repeater chain design and provide insights into the performance limits of first-generation quantum repeaters.

title: Optimal Control For Rydberg Multi-qubit Operations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents optimal control techniques for multi-qubit operations in Rydberg atom arrays, enhancing gate fidelity and scalability.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multi-qubit gates is challenging due to interactions and decoherence.
method: The authors develop optimal control protocols using gradient-based optimization to design pulse sequences that implement multi-qubit gates while minimizing errors.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity for two- and three-qubit operations compared to standard methods, with potential for scaling to larger systems.
conclusion: Optimal control enables high-fidelity multi-qubit operations in Rydberg systems, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With A Leakage From Digital-to-analog Conversion
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes the security impact of digital-to-analog converter leakage in continuous-variable quantum key distribution.
motivation: Practical CV-QKD systems use DACs for modulation, but DAC leakage can compromise security; this work quantifies the leakage and proposes countermeasures.
method: The authors model DAC leakage as an information leak to an eavesdropper and derive the resulting secret key rate under collective attacks using Gaussian optimality.
result: They show that DAC leakage can significantly reduce the achievable key rate, especially at high modulation variance, and that proper filtering can mitigate the effect.
conclusion: DAC leakage is a realistic security threat in CV-QKD that must be accounted for in practical implementations, but can be managed with appropriate design.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a cavity QED system.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical quantum devices.
method: Uses a cavity QED setup with a weak Kerr nonlinearity and engineered dissipation to prolong blockade duration.
result: Achieves photon blockade with significantly extended lifetime compared to conventional weak-nonlinearity schemes.
conclusion: Weak optical nonlinearities can be harnessed for effective photon blockade, enabling scalable quantum photonic devices.

title: Louvre: Relaxing Hardware Requirements Of Quantum Ldpc Codes By Routing With Expanded Quantum Instruction Set
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a routing-based approach to relax hardware connectivity requirements for quantum LDPC codes by expanding the quantum instruction set.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low-overhead fault tolerance but require high connectivity, which is challenging for near-term hardware. The authors aim to reduce these hardware demands.
method: They introduce an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling efficient implementation of LDPC codes on less connected qubit architectures.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the required qubit connectivity and physical qubit overhead while maintaining code performance.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a practical approach to make quantum LDPC codes more feasible on current and near-term quantum hardware.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; adaptive diversity can enhance performance by dynamically selecting transmission strategies.
method: The authors design adaptive diversity protocols that switch between spatial multiplexing and diversity modes based on channel state information, and optimize switching thresholds using convex optimization.
result: The proposed schemes achieve significant improvements in entanglement fidelity and throughput compared to non-adaptive approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising technique for practical quantum MIMO communication systems, offering robustness against channel variations.

title: Multiple Photons Enhance Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that using multiple photons in quantum machine learning can enhance performance, specifically in classification tasks using a photonic quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum machine learning often suffers from limited resources; using multiple photons may provide a practical advantage without requiring large-scale error correction.
method: The authors implement a quantum machine learning algorithm on a photonic chip, comparing single-photon and multi-photon inputs for classification tasks.
result: Multi-photon inputs yield higher classification accuracy and robustness to noise compared to single-photon inputs.
conclusion: Multiple photons can serve as a resource for enhancing quantum machine learning in near-term photonic devices.

title: Hidden Loop Currents In A Kagome Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and NMR reveal tiny internal magnetic fields in a kagome metal, indicating hidden loop currents consistent with an imaginary charge-density wave.
motivation: To uncover microscopic evidence of hidden electronic order in kagome metals, which may host exotic quantum states.
method: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance measurements to detect internal magnetic fields.
result: Observation of tiny internal magnetic fields providing microscopic evidence of spontaneous atomic-scale current loops.
conclusion: The findings support the existence of an imaginary charge-density wave order with loop currents in kagome metals.

title: Angular Momentum Of Rotating Fermionic Superfluids By Sagnac Phonon Interferometry
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper measures the angular momentum per particle in rotating fermionic superfluids across the BEC-BCS crossover using a Sagnac phonon interferometer.
motivation: To directly link fermionic pairing to macroscopic superflow and measure the quantum of angular momentum per particle.
method: A Sagnac-like phonon interferometer is used to probe the angular momentum of rotating fermionic superfluids.
result: Measurements of angular momentum per particle are achieved across the BEC-BCS crossover.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates a new way to probe superfluid properties in fermionic systems.

title: Anomalous Crossover From Three-dimensional Heisenberg To Two-dimensional Ising Magnetism In A Van Der Waals Magnet
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports an anomalous crossover from 3D Heisenberg to 2D Ising magnetism in a van der Waals magnet via self-intercalation.
motivation: Understanding how dimensionality and magnetic anisotropy affect magnetic order in low-dimensional systems is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use self-intercalation in Fe3GeTe2 to tune the magnetic interactions and characterize the magnetic ordering using experimental techniques.
result: They observe a crossover from three-dimensional Heisenberg to two-dimensional Ising ferromagnetism as a function of self-intercalation.
conclusion: Self-intercalation provides a new way to control magnetic dimensionality and anisotropy in van der Waals magnets.

title: Floquet Topological State Induced By Light-driven Band Inversion In SnTe
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Femtosecond light pulses induce a transient topological state in SnTe via band inversion.
motivation: To demonstrate light-driven topological phase transitions in semiconductors, which has been theoretically predicted but lacked clear experimental evidence.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are applied to SnTe, and the resulting electronic structure is probed using time-resolved angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES).
result: A transient topological state is observed that is absent at equilibrium, confirming light-induced band inversion.
conclusion: Light can be used to dynamically engineer topological phases in materials, opening avenues for ultrafast topological devices.

title: Creases As Information Bottlenecks In Active Elastic Sheets
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how creases in the active elastic sheet of the Trichoplax adhaerens animal act as information bottlenecks, coupling geometry to ciliary motion.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical folds in a living organism can control and constrain information flow in active matter systems.
method: Experimental observations and theoretical modeling of the feedback loop between crease geometry and collective ciliary motion in Trichoplax adhaerens.
result: Creases serve as information bottlenecks that regulate the collective behavior of cilia, enabling folding and unfolding dynamics.
conclusion: The study reveals a fundamental mechanism where geometry and active matter interact to process information in biological systems.

title: Fullqubit Alchemist: Quantum Algorithm For Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for alchemical free energy calculations, a method used in computational chemistry to compute free energy differences between molecular systems.
motivation: Alchemical free energy calculations are important for drug discovery and materials design but are computationally expensive on classical computers; quantum algorithms may offer speedups.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that combines Hamiltonian simulation with the alchemical transformation technique, using a hybrid quantum-classical approach to estimate free energy differences.
result: The algorithm demonstrates a potential quantum advantage for certain molecular systems, though practical implementation requires fault-tolerant quantum computers.
conclusion: Quantum computing can accelerate alchemical free energy calculations, but near-term applications are limited by hardware constraints.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper explains how tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy can probe lattice dynamics beyond elastic constants.
motivation: To provide insight into lattice dynamics using a specific spectroscopic technique.
method: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is used to measure phonon modes and lattice vibrations.
result: The technique reveals detailed information about lattice dynamics beyond standard elastic constants.
conclusion: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics in materials.

title: Geometric Phase Sensing Using Seismic Waves For Comprehensive Volcano Monitoring At Kı̄lauea Hawaii
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper applies geometric phase sensing from topological acoustics to seismic noise for volcano monitoring at Kīlauea.
motivation: To develop a new method for tracking volcanic activity using seismic waves, leveraging topological acoustics for subsurface sensing.
method: The authors use geometric phase sensing, a topological acoustics framework, to analyze seismic noise and extract subsurface changes over eruptive stages.
result: The method reveals subsurface changes across full eruptive stages, enabling comprehensive volcano monitoring.
conclusion: Geometric phase sensing is effective for monitoring dynamic Earth systems like volcanoes.

title: Ultrafast Photoreduction Driven By Interfacial Spin Exchange In Manganese-doped Quantum Dots
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: Manganese-doped quantum dots enable ultrafast electron transfer via spin exchange, driving photoreduction even when conventional charge transfer is unfavorable.
motivation: To understand and exploit hot-carrier photochemistry in quantum dots for efficient photocatalysis.
method: Synthesized Mn-doped quantum dots and measured ultrafast electron transfer to methyl viologen using transient absorption spectroscopy.
result: Spin exchange between Mn dopants and photogenerated carriers enables ultrafast photoreduction, bypassing band-edge limitations.
conclusion: Interfacial spin exchange is a key mechanism for hot-carrier extraction, offering new pathways for quantum dot-based photocatalysis.

title: Self-organized Nanoplasmonic Artificial Leaf For Hot-carrier Bioelectronic Interfaces
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a self-organized nanoplasmonic artificial leaf device for hot-carrier bioelectronic interfaces, enabling linear optoelectronic response and leadless multimodal modulation.
motivation: To develop a bioelectronic interface that can efficiently convert light into electrical signals for modulating biological systems without external leads.
method: The authors fabricate a nanoplasmonic artificial leaf using self-organized nanostructures that generate hot carriers upon light absorption, and characterize its optoelectronic performance.
result: The device exhibits linear performance over a wide range of light intensities and enables leadless, multimodal optoelectronic modulation and pixel-less optical pattern recognition.
conclusion: The self-organized nanoplasmonic artificial leaf offers a promising platform for bioelectronic interfaces with potential applications in optogenetics and neural modulation.

title: Deuterated Compounds For Organic Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: A review of deuterated compounds for organic light-emitting diodes, focusing on material advantages and mechanisms.
motivation: To survey recent advances in deuteration for improving OLED performance and stability.
method: Review of literature on deuterated organic semiconductors and their photophysical properties.
result: Deuteration can enhance device efficiency and lifetime by reducing non-radiative decay and improving charge transport.
conclusion: Deuterated compounds offer a promising route for next-generation OLEDs, but wider implementation requires further development.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: A technical review of data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology.
motivation: To compare regression-based, network-based, and decomposition techniques for extracting dynamical information from time-resolved biological data.
method: The review surveys and evaluates various data-driven approaches, including regression, neural networks, and decomposition methods, applied to biological systems.
result: It identifies strengths, limitations, and complementarity of different methods for modeling biological dynamics.
conclusion: Data-driven methods are powerful for biological modeling but require careful selection based on data characteristics and problem context.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective article discusses using radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore the potential of radioactive molecules as a platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics at energy scales complementary to colliders.
method: The paper reviews advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules, and discusses how these enable precision measurements.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei offer enhanced sensitivity to certain symmetry-violating effects, making them promising for fundamental physics tests.
conclusion: Advances in molecular quantum control and trapping are enabling a new class of precision experiments that can probe physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a method for depositing complex molecules onto surfaces for scanning tunnelling microscopy.
motivation: Imaging complex molecules with STM requires gentle deposition methods to avoid fragmentation.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to softly land intact molecules on a surface.
result: The method enables high-resolution STM imaging of complex molecules.
conclusion: Electrospray ion beam deposition is a viable technique for preparing samples of complex molecules for STM.

title: Forty Years Of Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A viewpoint article celebrating 40 years of atomic force microscopy, discussing its diverse applications and future developments.
motivation: To reflect on the impact and evolution of AFM as a key experimental technique across physics and other sciences.
method: Seven scientists provide their perspectives on how they use AFM and how they envision its future.
result: The article presents a collection of expert opinions on the current state and future directions of AFM.
conclusion: AFM remains a versatile and essential tool, with ongoing developments expected to expand its capabilities.

title: The Costs And Benefits Of Physics Research
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the environmental costs and benefits of physics research, advocating for cost-benefit analysis that includes environmental impacts.
motivation: To highlight the environmental footprint of physics research and encourage sustainable practices.
method: Commentary and opinion piece, likely reviewing existing literature and proposing a framework for cost-benefit analysis.
result: Argues that environmental impacts should be considered in decisions about which physics research to pursue.
conclusion: Physics research should incorporate environmental cost-benefit analysis to reduce its ecological footprint.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A commentary on the evolution of atomic force microscopy from imaging to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the broad impact and versatility of AFM beyond surface imaging.
method: Historical review and commentary on key innovations in AFM technology.
result: AFM has become a multipurpose tool for nanoscale characterization.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its role in nanoscience and beyond.

title: The Relative Effectiveness Of Active Learning Methods
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: A multi-institutional study comparing the effectiveness of four active learning methods in introductory physics classrooms.
motivation: To determine which active learning methods are most effective for physics education, as their comparative effectiveness is unclear.
method: Multi-institutional study comparing four well-established active learning methods in introductory physics courses.
result: The study provides comparative effectiveness data for the four methods.
conclusion: The findings help educators choose the most effective active learning strategies for physics instruction.

title: The Physical Consequences Of Sperm Gigantism
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the physical consequences of sperm gigantism in fruit flies, showing that reciprocal pushing between thousands of sperm maintains them in a motile and unentangled state.
motivation: To understand how extremely long sperm (longer than the storage sac) remain motile and unentangled, which is a biological puzzle.
method: Experimental observations and theoretical modeling of sperm dynamics in the Drosophila seminal vesicle.
result: Reciprocal pushing interactions between sperm prevent entanglement and maintain motility.
conclusion: Physical interactions, not just biological mechanisms, are crucial for sperm storage and function.

title: Overcoming The Fill-factor Limit Of Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper addresses the fill-factor limit in organic solar cells through a guest-host design that prolongs exciton lifetime, improving both fill factor and open-circuit voltage.
motivation: Organic solar cells suffer from field-dependent charge generation due to exciton/charge-transfer coupling, which limits their fill factor and overall efficiency.
method: The authors combine modeling with a novel guest-host material design to extend exciton lifetime, thereby reducing field-dependent losses.
result: The proposed design simultaneously raises the fill factor and open-circuit voltage, overcoming the traditional fill-factor limit.
conclusion: The guest-host approach offers a pathway to higher efficiency organic solar cells by addressing the exciton/charge-transfer coupling issue.

title: Super-Snell Scanning Light-field Display For Ultrawide-angle High-resolution Glasses-free Three-dimensional Displays
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A scanning light-field display achieving ultrawide-angle, high-resolution glasses-free 3D display using the Snell's window effect.
motivation: To overcome the trade-off between viewing angle and resolution in glasses-free 3D displays.
method: A super-Snell scanning light-field architecture that exploits Snell's window effect to expand the viewing angle while maintaining high resolution.
result: Demonstrated a 150° viewing angle and nearly 480-pixel resolution in a prototype.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables practical ultrawide-angle, high-resolution glasses-free 3D displays.

title: Author Correction: Single-shot Terahertz-field-driven X-ray Streak Camera
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This is an author correction for a paper on a terahertz-field-driven X-ray streak camera, which is an ultrafast measurement technique in X-ray science.
motivation: The original paper presented a method for single-shot X-ray pulse characterization using terahertz fields, important for ultrafast X-ray experiments.
method: The correction likely addresses errors or updates in the original publication.
result: No new scientific results; it is a correction notice.
conclusion: The paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wide-temperature-range Fluid-phase Grain Boundaries For Temperature-robust Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to improve perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability using fluid-phase grain boundaries.
motivation: Perovskite solar cells suffer from thermal cycling instability due to grain boundary defects; the authors aim to enhance durability and efficiency.
method: They introduce a wide-temperature-range fluid-phase molecular complex that forms dynamically adaptive grain boundaries in perovskite films.
result: The approach achieves an efficiency of 26.52% and improved thermal cycling stability.
conclusion: Fluid-phase grain boundaries offer a promising route to temperature-robust perovskite solar cells.

title: A Super-inert Near-infrared Fluorescent Rotaxane Dye For Surgical Navigation
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: A near-infrared fluorescent rotaxane dye with high photostability and renal clearance is developed for surgical navigation imaging.
motivation: Current near-infrared dyes suffer from photobleaching and non-specific binding, limiting their use in surgical navigation.
method: A threaded α-cyclodextrin rotaxane structure is used to create a NIR dye with enhanced photostability and solubility.
result: The dye enables ureter imaging in mice and pigs via NIR-II and clinical NIR-I laparoscopes with negligible non-specific binding.
conclusion: This rotaxane dye offers a practical solution for real-time surgical navigation with improved imaging performance.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A review of the physics of GaN-based LEDs, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: GaN-based LEDs are crucial for modern lighting, but their efficiency is governed by complex physical effects that need to be understood.
method: The review synthesizes existing research on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects in GaN LEDs.
result: The paper describes how these three effects impact LED performance, including efficiency droop and emission wavelength.
conclusion: Understanding these physical mechanisms is key to further improving GaN LED efficiency and design.

title: Electrochemical Direct Air Capture By Local Alkalinity Generation At Three-dimensional Interfaces
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents an electrochemical platform for direct air capture of CO2 using a three-dimensional reactive interface.
motivation: Direct air capture of CO2 is a scalable route to mitigate climate change, but current methods often have high energy consumption and low capture rates.
method: The authors design a three-dimensional reactive interface that generates local alkalinity electrochemically to enhance CO2 capture from air.
result: The platform achieves high capture rates with competitive energy consumption compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The proposed electrochemical direct air capture method offers a promising scalable solution for atmospheric CO2 removal.

title: Single-cell Analyses Identify The Ginseng Embryonic Protoderm As A Native Compartment For High-efficiency Ginsenoside Production
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses single-cell analyses to identify the ginseng embryonic protoderm as a compartment for high-efficiency ginsenoside production, and develops epigenetic and genetic strategies to enhance metabolite output.
motivation: To find a scalable and sustainable alternative to conventional field cultivation of ginsenosides, which are valuable plant natural products.
method: Single-cell RNA sequencing and other single-cell analyses were performed on ginseng embryos to identify cell types; then epigenetic and genetic engineering strategies were applied to boost ginsenoside production.
result: The embryonic protoderm was identified as a native compartment with high ginsenoside production capacity, and the engineered strategies significantly increased yield.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for sustainable production of ginsenosides using plant cell cultures, bypassing traditional field cultivation.

title: Diverse Radical Transformations Of Allenic C(sp)–C(sp<sup>2</sup>) And C(sp<sup>3</sup>)–C(sp<sup>2</sup>) Bonds Enabled By Silyl Substitution
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents base metal-catalyzed radical cleavage of allenic C(sp)–C(sp2) and C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds using air as an oxidant, enabled by silyl substitution.
motivation: The oxidative cleavage of olefins is well established, but radical-mediated chemo- and regioselective cleavage of allene carbon-carbon bonds remains a challenge in synthetic chemistry.
method: The authors developed a base metal-catalyzed protocol that utilizes air as an oxidant and silyl substitution to achieve selective cleavage of allenic C(sp)–C(sp2) double bonds and C(sp3)–C(sp2) single bonds.
result: The method enables diverse radical transformations of allenic carbon-carbon bonds with high chemo- and regioselectivity.
conclusion: This work provides a new strategy for cleaving allenic bonds, expanding the toolbox of synthetic organic chemistry.

title: Spatially Explicit Temperature Optima Improve Climate Impact Assessment Of Global Crop Productivity
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper maps spatially explicit temperature optima for staple crops to improve climate impact assessments of global crop productivity.
motivation: Current agricultural climate models use constant optimal temperatures globally, ignoring local adaptation, leading to inaccurate predictions.
method: The authors compile and analyze spatially explicit data on temperature optima for four major staple crops and incorporate them into a global crop model.
result: The spatially explicit optima significantly improve predictions of future crop productivity under climate change scenarios.
conclusion: Accounting for local adaptation of crops to temperature is crucial for reliable climate impact assessments.

title: Ligand-controlled Sequential Activation Enables Nickel-catalysed Alkyl–alkynyl Coupling
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a nickel-catalysed cross-electrophile coupling reaction for forming alkyl–alkynyl bonds, enabled by a tridentate ligand that controls the sequence of electrophile activation.
motivation: The coupling between unactivated alkyl halides and alkynyl halides has been challenging due to reactivity mismatch and poor chemoselectivity; the authors aim to develop a selective catalytic method.
method: The authors use a nickel catalyst with a tridentate ligand to sequentially activate the two electrophiles, enabling the cross-coupling.
result: The method allows direct construction of alkynyl–alkyl bonds with high chemoselectivity.
conclusion: This work provides a new strategy for alkyl–alkynyl coupling, expanding the scope of nickel-catalysed cross-electrophile reactions.

title: A Fourth Subgenome Of The Camelina Genus Reveals Gene Dominance Is Influenced By Chromosomal Proximity
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents genome assemblies of tetraploid and hexaploid Camelina species, revealing that gene dominance is influenced by chromosomal proximity.
motivation: To complete the genome assembly of the ploidy series in the Camelina genus and understand the mechanisms of gene dominance in polyploid plants.
method: The authors assembled genomes of a tetraploid and two hexaploid C. microcarpa accessions, along with the cultivated hexaploid C. sativa, using sequencing and comparative genomics.
result: They found that gene dominance is influenced by chromosomal proximity, providing insights into polyploid genome evolution.
conclusion: Chromosomal proximity plays a key role in gene dominance in polyploid Camelina species, advancing understanding of plant genome evolution.
